:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0,$ $x=1,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=1,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $\mathbf{F} =e^z \, \mathbf{i} + x^2y^2 \, \mathbf{j} + 4x^2yz \, \mathbf{k},$ find the flux of $\mathbf{F}$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
\iint\limits_{S} \mathbf{F}\cdot\mathrm{d}\mathbf{S}
= \iiint\limits_R \textrm{div}\,\mathbf{F} \: \textrm{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $\mathbf{F},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{z})+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(4{x}^{2}yz) \\  & =0+2{x}^{2}y+4{x}^{2}y \\  & =6{x}^{2}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}2y\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{3}]_{x=0}^{x=1}\cdot [{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=2}\cdot (2-1) \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (4-0)\cdot 1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+y) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z+0+0 \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=2}\cdot (1-0)\cdot [\operatorname{sin}⁡z]_{z=0}^{z=\pi /2} \\  & =({2}^{2}-{0}^{2})\cdot 1\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0,$ $x=2,$ $y=0,$ $y=4,$ $z=1,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F={x}^{2}y\,i+2z\,j+xyz\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz) \\  & =2xy+0+xy \\  & =3xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}3xy\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}3xy\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{4}y\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{1}^{2}3\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=4}\cdot [3z]_{z=1}^{z=2} \\  & =(2-0)\cdot (8-0)\cdot (6-3) \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=e,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=0,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=y\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,i+{z}^{2}\,j+(x-{y}^{3})\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x-{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{y}{x}+0+0 \\  & =\frac{y}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}z \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{x=1}^{x=e}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\cdot [z]_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡e-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot (\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2})\cdot (2-0) \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (2-0) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0,$ $x=1,$ $y=1,$ $y=2,$ $z=1,$ $z=3.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F={x}^{2}\,i+2y\,j+(x+{y}^{2})\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+{y}^{2}) \\  & =2x+2+0 \\  & =2x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(2x+2)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}(2x+2)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+2)\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}+2x]_{x=0}^{x=1}\cdot (2-1)\cdot (3-1) \\  & =({1}^{2}+2(1)-0)\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0,$ $x=1,$ $y=1,$ $y=2,$ $z=-1,$ $z=1.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=2y\,i+x{y}^{2}\,j+2xyz\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2xyz) \\  & =0+2xy+2xy \\  & =4xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}4xy\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}4xy\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{1}^{2}2y\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=1}\cdot [{y}^{2}]_{y=1}^{y=2}\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (4-1)\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=3,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=-1,$ $z=1.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(y-{x}^{2})\,i+xy\,j+3xz\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-{x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3xz) \\  & =(-2x)+x+3x \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}2x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=3}\cdot (2-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =(9-1)\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=-1,$ $x=1,$ $y=0,$ $y=3,$ $z=1,$ $z=3.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(2{x}^{3}+z)\,i-z\,j-3{x}^{2}z\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{3}+z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3{x}^{2}z) \\  & =6{x}^{2}+0+(-3{x}^{2}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3{x}^{2}\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{3}]_{x=-1}^{x=1}\cdot (3-0)\cdot (3-1) \\  & =({1}^{3}-(-1)^{3})\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=-1,$ $x=2,$ $y=0,$ $y=1,$ $z=-1,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=y{z}^{2}\,i-2yz\,j+3{z}^{2}\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2yz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3{z}^{2}) \\  & =0+(-2z)+6z \\  & =4z.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}4z\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}4z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{2}4z\,\text{d}z \\  & =(2-(-1))\cdot (1-0)\cdot [2{z}^{2}]_{z=-1}^{z=2} \\  & =3\cdot 1\cdot (8-2) \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0,$ $x=1,$ $y=1,$ $y=3,$ $z=0,$ $z=\operatorname{ln}⁡3.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(y+{z}^{2})\,i-x\,j+3{x}^{2}{e}^{z}\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y+{z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-x)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3{x}^{2}{e}^{z}) \\  & =0+0+3{x}^{2}{e}^{z} \\  & =3{x}^{2}{e}^{z}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}3{x}^{2}{e}^{z}\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}3{x}^{2}{e}^{z}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{e}^{z}\,\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{3}]_{x=0}^{x=1}\cdot (3-1)\cdot [{e}^{z}]_{z=0}^{z=\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =({1}^{3}-{0}^{3})\cdot 2\cdot ({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot (3-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
